Uncle wishes me out of the way; thinks I ought to go, and, sooner or later, will tell me so. I don’t intend to wait for that, but, like the people in fairy tales, travel away into the world and seek my fortune.

arxiv-1903-10630.title: Diversifying Reply Suggestions using a Matching-Conditional Variational Autoencoder
arxiv-1903-10630.creator: Budhaditya Deb, Peter Bailey, Milad Shokouhi
arxiv-1903-10630.description: Abstract We consider the problem of diversifying automated reply suggestions for a commercial instant-messaging (IM) system (Skype). Our conversation model is a standard matching based information retrieval architecture, which consists of two parallel encoders to project messages and replies into a common feature representation.

arxiv-2103-05116.title: ASL to PET Translation by a Semi-supervised Residual-based Attention-guided Convolutional Neural Network
arxiv-2103-05116.creator: Sahar Yousefi, Hessam Sokooti, Wouter M. Teeuwisse, Dennis F.R. Heijtel, Aart J. Nederveen, Marius Staring, Matthias J.P. van Osch
arxiv-2103-05116.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Sahar Yousefi, Hessam Sokooti, Wouter M. Teeuwisse, Dennis F.R. Heijtel, Aart J. Nederveen, Marius Staring, Matthias J.P. van Osch. Positron Emission Tomography (PET) is an imaging method that can assess physiological function rather than structural disturbances by measuring cerebral perfusion or glucose consumption. However, this imaging technique relies on injection of radioactive tracers and is expensive. On the contrary, Arterial Spin Labeling (ASL) MRI is a non-invasive, non-radioactive, and relatively cheap imaging technique for brain hemodynamic measurements, which allows quantification to some extent.

arxiv-2109-09521.title: RibSeg Dataset and Strong Point Cloud Baselines for Rib Segmentation from CT Scans
arxiv-2109-09521.creator: Jiancheng Yang, Shixuan Gu, Donglai Wei, Hanspeter Pfister, Bingbing Ni
arxiv-2109-09521.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jiancheng Yang, Shixuan Gu, Donglai Wei, Hanspeter Pfister, Bingbing Ni. Manual rib inspections in computed tomography (CT) scans are clinically critical but labor-intensive, as 24 ribs are typically elongated and oblique in 3D volumes. Automatic rib segmentation methods can speed up the process through rib measurement and visualization. However, prior arts mostly use in-house labeled datasets that are publicly unavailable and work on dense 3D volumes that are computationally inefficient.

arxiv-2211-09415.title: Near-Optimal Distributed Computation of Small Vertex Cuts
arxiv-2211-09415.creator: Merav Parter, Asaf Petruschka
arxiv-2211-09415.description: Abstract We present near-optimal algorithms for detecting small vertex cuts in the 𝖢𝖮𝖭𝖦𝖤𝖲𝖳 {\mathsf{CONGEST}} model of distributed computing. Despite extensive research in this area, our understanding of the vertex connectivity of a graph is still incomplete, especially in the distributed setting.

arxiv-2308-14418.title: Multiscale and Multilayer Contrastive Learning for Domain Generalization
arxiv-2308-14418.creator: Aristotelis Ballas, Christos Diou
arxiv-2308-14418.description: Abstract During the past decade, deep neural networks have led to fast-paced progress and significant achievements in computer vision problems, for both academia and industry. Yet despite their success, state-of-the-art image classification approaches fail to generalize well in previously unseen visual contexts, as required by many real-world applications.

arxiv-2311-09168.title: Arkade: k-Nearest Neighbor Search With Non-Euclidean Distances using GPU Ray Tracing Conference: Proceedings of the 38th ACM International Conference on Supercomputing; June 4–7, 2024; Kyoto, Japan Proceedings of the 38th ACM International Conference on Supercomputing (ICS ’24), June 4–7, 2024, Kyot
arxiv-2311-09168.creator: Durga Mandarapu, Vani Nagarajan, Artem Pelenitsyn, Milind Kulkarni
arxiv-2311-09168.description: Abstract . High-performance implementations of k k -Nearest Neighbor Search ( k k NN) in low dimensions use tree-based data structures. Tree algorithms are hard to parallelize on GPUs due to their irregularity. However, newer Nvidia GPUs offer hardware support for tree operations through ray-tracing cores.

arxiv-2402-01541.title: The galactic bubbles of starburst galaxies
arxiv-2402-01541.creator: Z. Meliani, P. Cristofari, A. Rodríguez-González, G. Fichet de Clairfontaine, E. Proust, E. Peretti
arxiv-2402-01541.description: Abstract Context. The galactic winds of starburst galaxies (SBGs) give rise to remarkable structures on kiloparsec scales. However, the evolution and shape of these giant wind bubbles, as well as the properties of the shocks they develop, are not yet fully understood. Aims.

arxiv-2402-15016.title: A stochastic moving ball approximation method for smooth convex constrained minimization
arxiv-2402-15016.creator: Nitesh Kumar Singh, Ion Necoara
arxiv-2402-15016.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Nitesh Kumar Singh, Ion Necoara. In this paper, we consider constrained optimization problems with convex objective and smooth convex constraints. We propose a new stochastic gradient algorithm, called the Stochastic Moving Ball Approximation (SMBA) method, to solve this class of problems, where at each iteration we first take a (sub)gradient step for the objective function and then perform a projection step onto one ball approximation of a randomly chosen constraint.

arxiv-2411-01457.title: Facet-Aware Multi-Head Mixture-of-Experts Model for Sequential Recommendation
arxiv-2411-01457.creator: Mingrui Liu, Sixiao Zhang, Cheng Long
arxiv-2411-01457.description: Abstract . Sequential recommendation (SR) systems excel at capturing users’ dynamic preferences by leveraging their interaction histories. Most existing SR systems assign a single embedding vector to each item to represent its features, and various types of models are adopted to combine these item embeddings into a sequence representation vector to capture the user intent.

arxiv-2501-07354.title: Enhancing the sensitivity of single-microwave-photon detection with bandwidth tunability.
arxiv-2501-07354.creator: Louis Pallegoix 1 , Jaime Travesedo 1 , Alexandre S. May 1,2 , Léo Balembois 1 , Denis Vion 1 , Patrice Bertet* 1 and Emmanuel Flurin*
arxiv-2501-07354.description: Abstract We report on the characteristics of a microwave photon counter device based on a superconducting transmon qubit. Its design is similar to [ 4 ] , with an additional bandwidth tuning circuit that permits tuning the detection bandwidth over an order of magnitude to optimize the device efficiency and noise.

arxiv-2502-11314.title: A note on some high-dimensional handlebodies
arxiv-2502-11314.creator: Geunyoung Kim
arxiv-2502-11314.description: Abstract . For k ≥ 0 k\geq 0 and n ≥ 2 ​ k + 1 n\geq 2k+1 , we show that every n n -dimensional k k -handlebody is the product of a 2 ​ k 2k -dimensional k k -handlebody and the standard ( n − 2 ​ k ) (n-2k) -ball.

arxiv-2506-22644.title: Evaluating Hybrid Retrieval Augmented Generation using Dynamic Test Sets: LiveRAG Challenge
arxiv-2506-22644.creator: Chase Fensore † \dagger , Kaustubh Dhole † \dagger , Joyce Ho ∗ , Eugene Agichtein ∗
arxiv-2506-22644.description: Abstract . We present our submission to the LiveRAG Challenge 2025, which evaluates retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems on dynamic test sets using the FineWeb-10BT corpus. Our final hybrid approach combines sparse (BM25) and dense (E5) retrieval methods and then aims to generate relevant and faithful answers with Falcon3-10B-Instruct.

arxiv-2509-00841.title: Neural Models and Language Model Prompting for the Multidimensional Evaluation of Open-Ended Conversations
arxiv-2509-00841.creator: Michelle Elizabeth, Alicja Kasicka, Natalia Krawczyk, Magalie Ochs, Gwénolé Lecorvé, Justyna Gromada, Lina M. Rojas-Barahona
arxiv-2509-00841.description: Abstract The growing number of generative AI-based dialogue systems has made their evaluation a crucial challenge. This paper presents our contribution to this important problem through the Dialogue System Technology Challenge (DSTC-12, Track 1), where we developed models to predict dialogue-level, dimension-specific scores. Given the constraint of using relatively small models (i.e.

arxiv-2601-01016.title: Improving Variational Autoencoder using Random Fourier Transformation: An Aviation Safety Anomaly Detection Case-Study
arxiv-2601-01016.creator: Ata Akbari Asanjan, Milad Memarzadeh, Bryan Matthews, Nikunj Oza
arxiv-2601-01016.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Ata Akbari Asanjan, Milad Memarzadeh, Bryan Matthews, Nikunj Oza. In this study, we focus on the training process and inference improvements of deep neural networks (DNNs), specifically Autoencoders (AEs) and Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), using Random Fourier Transformation (RFT).

arxiv-2602-23594.title: Who Matters to Whom? Identifying Peer Effects with Propagation Geometry
arxiv-2602-23594.creator: Guy Tchuente
arxiv-2602-23594.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Guy Tchuente. This paper develops a unifying theory of peer effects that treats the peer aggregator (the social norm mapping peers’ actions into a scalar exposure) as the central behavioral primitive. We formulate peer influence as a norm game in which payoffs depend on own action and an exposure index, and we provide equilibrium existence and uniqueness for a broad class of aggregators.

pmc-10480157.title: Quantitative detection of formaldehyde using solid phase microextraction gas chromatography–mass spectrometry coupled to cysteamine scavenging
pmc-10480157.creator: Sara Y. Chothia, Matthew Carr, Paul S. Monks, Rebecca L. Cordell, Richard J. Hopkinson
pmc-10480157.description: Formaldehyde (HCHO) is a toxic and carcinogenic pollutant and human metabolite that reacts with biomolecules under physiological conditions. Quantifying HCHO is essential for ongoing biological and biomedical research on HCHO; however, its reactivity, small size and volatility make this challenging. Here, we report a novel HCHO detection/quantification method that couples cysteamine-mediated HCHO scavenging with SPME GC–MS analysis.

pmc-10650899.title: Mild Cardiotoxicity and Continued Trastuzumab Treatment in the Context of HER2-Positive Breast Cancer
pmc-10650899.creator: Orianne de la Brassinne Bonardeaux, Benjamin Born, Marie Moonen, Patrizio Lancellotti, Tong Liu
pmc-10650899.description: Breast cancer is the leading cause of cancer death in women worldwide. Trastuzumab, the main HER2-targeted treatment, faces limitations due to potential cardiotoxicity. The management of patients with mild cardiotoxicity on trastuzumab remains uncertain, resulting in treatment discontinuation and negative oncological outcomes. This retrospective study analyzed 23 patients who experienced decreased left ventricular function during trastuzumab treatment.

pmc-11436056.title: Oxytocin: A Shield against Radiation-Induced Lung Injury in Rats
pmc-11436056.creator: Ahmet Kayalı, Duygu Burcu Arda, Ejder Saylav Bora, Yiğit Uyanikgil, Özüm Atasoy, Oytun Erbaş, Barbara Ruaro, Yusuke Inoue
pmc-11436056.description: Background: Radiation-induced lung injury (RILI), a serious side effect of thoracic radiotherapy, can lead to acute radiation pneumonitis (RP) and chronic pulmonary fibrosis (PF). Despite various interventions, no effective protocol exists to prevent pneumonitis. Oxytocin (OT), known for its anti-inflammatory, antiapoptotic, and antioxidant properties, has not been explored for its potential in mitigating RILI.

pmc-11488585.title: USP10 promotes pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma progression by attenuating FOXC1 protein degradation to activate the WNT signaling pathway
pmc-11488585.creator: Jie Wang, Lang Gan, Fenghao Liu, Qin Yang, Qingsong Deng, Di Jiang, Chengcheng Zhang, LeiDa Zhang, XiaoJun Wang
pmc-11488585.description: Increasing evidence has suggested that ubiquitin-specific protease 10 (USP10), a deubiquitinating enzyme, plays an essential role in targeted protein degradation and participates in cancer progression. However, the relationship between USP10 and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is poorly understood. Here, we developed a USP-targeting siRNA library, combining a loss-of-function experimental screen in patient-derived PDAC cells.

pmc-11502676.title: Lonely, stressed-out moms
pmc-11502676.creator: Elena Bridgers, Molly M Fox
pmc-11502676.description: Perinatal mood and anxiety disorders (PMADs) are estimated to affect as many as 17.7% of mothers in agricultural and postindustrial societies. Various lines of research converge to suggest that PMADs may be ‘diseases of modernity’, arising from a mismatch between the environments in which humans evolved over hundreds of thousands of years and contemporary postindustrial lifestyles.

pmc-12417586.title: Bilateral Oculomotor Nerve Palsy: A Rare Complication of Bridging Thrombolysis for Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion
pmc-12417586.creator: Shuangyun Lv, Ronghui Liu, Jiapeng Sun, Hongmei Liu, Xin Guo, Changxia Ding
pmc-12417586.description: Acute vertebrobasilar artery occlusion (AVBAO) accounts for only 1–2% of ischemic stroke, but it has high disability and mortality rates. Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) combined with intravenous thrombolysis can quickly achieve vascular recanalization and significantly improve patient prognosis. This report describes a 73-year-old male who was admitted to the hospital in a coma due to AVBAO.

pmc-12495988.title: Investigating the role of tripartite motif containing-21 and interleukin-6 in pro-Inflammatory symptom-associated heterogeneity within primary Sjögren’s syndrome
pmc-12495988.creator: Lauren R Scott, Joe Berry, Kyle Thompson, Jessica Tarn, Karl Wood, John Casement, Wan-Fai Ng
pmc-12495988.description: Background and ObjectivesIn Primary Sjögren’s Syndrome (pSS) clinical heterogeneity is a challenge to both treatment and disease understanding. Variations in symptoms may be driven by different underlying biological pathways. Tripartite motif containing-21 (TRIM21) and interleukin-6 (IL-6) have been implicated in autoimmunity and inflammation, with links to chronic interferon activity.

pmc-12528442.title: Effect of listening to preferred music at different frequencies during warmup on physical performance and psychophysiological responses in male athletes
pmc-12528442.creator: Nidhal Jebabli, Manar Boujabli, Ibrahim Ouergui, Nejmeddine Ouerghi, Fatma Hilal Yagin, Burak Yagin, Mariem Khlifi, Anissa Bouassida, Abderraouf Ben Abderrahman, Safaa M Elkholi
pmc-12528442.description: The present study assessed the effects of listening to preferred music during warm-up at different frequencies (440 Hz vs. 432 Hz) on the physical performance and psychophysiological responses in male athletes. In a double-blind crossover study design, twenty-two male athletes (Mean ± SD: age: 22.4 ± 1.6 years; body mass: 71.8 ± 8.3 kg; height: 1.83 ± 0.

pmc-12559024.title: Proposal Writing Training and Idea Development for Early‐Career Researchers Based on Constructive Alignment, Co‐Creation and Active Learning Strategies
pmc-12559024.creator: Friederike Hoffmann, Mahaut de Vareilles, Linling Chen, Catherine Downy, Nadine Goris
pmc-12559024.description: In today's research landscape, which is ever more dependent on external funding, early career researchers (ECRs) urgently need competence in idea development and proposal writing. However, generalized lectures provided by many higher education and research institutions lack practical elements such as hands‐on skill training and support measures to coach the ECRs through the process of developing their own proposal.

pmc-12670460.title: Artificial Intelligence–Based Computerized Digit Vigilance Test in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: Development and Validation Study
pmc-12670460.creator: Gong-Hong Lin, Dorothy Bai, Yi-Jing Huang, Shih-Chieh Lee, Mai Thi Thuy Vu, Tsu-Hsien Chiu, Andrew Coristine
pmc-12670460.description: BackgroundThe Computerized Digit Vigilance Test (CDVT) is a well-established measure of sustained attention. However, the CDVT only measures the total reaction time and response accuracy and fails to capture other crucial attentional features such as the eye blink rate, yawns, head movements, and eye movements. Omitting such features might provide an incomplete representative picture of sustained attention.

pmc-12993332.title: Staged conversion after circular ring external fixation in adult open long-bone fractures: A systematic review☆
pmc-12993332.creator: Domenico Fenga, Daniel Pérez-Prieto, Gabriele Giuca, Paolo Rizzo, Biagio Zampogna, Danilo Leonetti
pmc-12993332.description: BackgroundCircular ring external fixation is frequently used in high-energy open long-bone fractures, yet prolonged frame retention is associated with pin-tract morbidity and patient burden. Staged conversion to internal fixation is therefore attractive, but concerns persist regarding deep infection and nonunion.

pmc-13254180.title: Impact of red blood cell transfusion and transfusion strategies on clinical outcomes in extremely low gestational age neonates
pmc-13254180.creator: Xuejing Liu, Junling Ma, Fangrui Ding
pmc-13254180.description: ObjectiveTo investigate the effects of red blood cell transfusions and transfusion strategies on clinical outcomes in extremely low gestational age neonates (ELGANs).MethodsThis retrospective cohort study enrolled 545 ELGANs with gestational age <28 weeks admitted between 2012 and 2024. Infants were divided into transfusion and non-transfusion groups.

pmc-13410872.title: Trends in cardiovascular mortality among lung cancer patients in the United States: a retrospective study from 1999 to 2023
pmc-13410872.creator: Yong-li Chen, Jian-quan Chen, Lin-wen Zeng, Jin-yan Wu, Xiao‐xia Qiu, Zhen-nan Lin, Jie Xiao, Xing Miao, Re‐hua Wang, Jian‐cheng Zhang
pmc-13410872.description: BackgroundAlthough cardiovascular disease (CVD) frequently co-occurs with lung cancer and adversely affects prognosis, the temporal patterns of CVD mortality in this patient group remain inadequately explored. We aimed to clarify trends and disparities in CVD mortality among United States (US) adults with lung cancer.
